mainTopic: Buying a tree and the land under it, the owner's duty to protest (מחאה), and the משנה about three regions for חזקה with the גמרא's analysis of protest made away from the holder
overview: The גמרא finishes discussing someone who buys a tree. רבא objects that the seller could say he sold only a small plant to be pulled up. So רבא limits the ruling to a buyer who claims the land was part of the deal. מר קשישא asks רב אשי what an honest seller can do, and the answer is that he should have protested (מחאה). The גמרא proves this from the mortgages of סורא, since the Rabbis would not set up a system that leads to loss. A new משנה then teaches that יהודה, עבר הירדן and גליל are separate regions for חזקה. רבי יהודה explains that the three years exist so that even an owner far away can hear the news and come back. The גמרא asks what the first opinion holds about a protest made when the holder is not present. רב answers that the משנה speaks of a time of crisis, and the גמרא begins to explain why it names יהודה and גליל, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבא objects: maybe only a small plant was sold
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges the earlier ruling that the buyer of a tree gets the land under it. The seller can say he only sold a plant to be uprooted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected: Let the seller say to the buyer, 'I sold you a saffron crocus. Pull up the saffron crocus and go!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the earlier ruling that buying a tree also gives you the ground under it. He says the seller can claim he sold only the plant, not the land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A saffron crocus is a small plant that the buyer pulls up and takes away, so it comes with no land. רבא's point is that selling something that grows does not have to include the soil. So why should the tree buyer automatically get the land?

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it (a strong challenge)
A saffron crocus, a small plant that gets uprooted

phrases.english: Rava objects to it:
But let [the seller] say to him:
"I sold you a saffron crocus,"
phrases.notes: He means: I sold you only the plant, which gets pulled up, not the ground it grows in.

phrases.english: "Uproot the saffron crocus and go!"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling stated just before this section, that a tree buyer gets the land beneath it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that buying a tree automatically includes the land under it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A seller can sell a growing plant with no land at all, like a crocus, so the land is not automatically part of the sale.

steps.title: רבא: the ruling applies only when the buyer makes a specific claim
steps.stepSummary: רבא changes the scope of the ruling. The buyer gets the land only when he claims the land was part of the deal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: The ruling is about a buyer who comes with a claim.
steps.whatsHappening: Because of his own objection, רבא limits the earlier ruling. The buyer gets the land only if he claims he was specifically sold it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא shows that רבא is replacing the simple reading of the ruling. Without a claim, the buyer does not get the land. If he holds it and claims the seller agreed to include the land, he can be believed.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, instead (the earlier reading is being replaced)
Comes with a claim, backs up his holding with an argument

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
It is in a case where he comes with a claim.
phrases.notes: The buyer claims the seller agreed to include the land under the tree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves רבא's own objection by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to a buyer who makes a specific claim
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every tree buyer automatically gets the land beneath it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a buyer who claims the land was included gets it.

steps.title: מר קשישא asks: what can an honest seller do?
steps.stepSummary: מר קשישא בריה דרב חסדא asks רב אשי how a seller who really sold only the tree can protect himself from such a claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר קשישא, son of רב חסדא, said to רב אשי: And if the seller really did sell him only a saffron crocus, what should he have done?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question comes up. If the buyer can win just by claiming, how can a seller who truly sold only the plant protect his land?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's answer seems to leave the seller helpless, since any buyer could make up a claim. מר קשישא wants to know what step the seller should take. This sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: מר קשישא, son of רב חסדא

phrases.english: Mar Kashisha
son of Rav Chisda, said to Rav Ashi:
And if he really sold him only a saffron crocus,
what should he have done?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר קַשִּׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא לְרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the fairness of רבא's narrowed ruling from the seller's side.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can a seller who truly sold only the tree stop the buyer from claiming the land?

steps.title: The answer: he should have protested
steps.stepSummary: The seller should have made a protest (מחאה) so the buyer's holding would not become a חזקה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a short answer to מר קשישא: the seller should have protested. If he did not, he has only himself to blame.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מחאה is a public statement that the land is still his. Once he protests, the buyer's time on the land does not turn into proof of ownership. So the seller is not helpless.

phrases.english: He should have protested.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The seller should have protested against the buyer's holding of the land.

steps.title: Proof from the mortgages of סורא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that protest is the answer. Otherwise the lender in a סורא mortgage could hide the document and claim he bought the land, and the owner would lose it.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you do not say so, look at the mortgages of סורא, which are written: 'When these years are over, this land goes back without money.' If the lender hid the mortgage document and said, 'I bought this land,' would he really be believed? Would the Rabbis set up an arrangement that leads people to a loss?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof that protesting must be the solution. It uses a well-known type of mortgage from סורא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a סורא mortgage the lender holds the land for a set number of years, and then it goes back to the owner for free. If the lender hid the document and claimed he bought the land, the owner would lose it unless protesting helps. Since the Rabbis would not set up a system that causes loss, the owner must have a way out, and that way is protest.

keyTerms.meaning: For if you do not say so (introduces a proof)

phrases.english: For if you do not say so,
these mortgages of Sura—
in which it is written like this:
"At the completion of these years,
this land will go out without money";
phrases.notes: It goes back to the owner, and he does not have to pay anything.

phrases.english: if [the lender] hides the mortgage document,
and says: "It is bought, and that is why it is in my hand"—
would he really be believed?!
Would the Rabbis set up an arrangement
that leads people to a loss?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer that the owner should have protested.
steps.raayaObject: That protest is what protects an owner from someone who holds his land and claims it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The standard mortgage arrangement of סורא, which the Rabbis would not have set up if it led to loss.

steps.title: So too here, he should have protested
steps.stepSummary: Just as the owner in the סורא mortgage must protest, the seller of the tree also should have protested.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he should have protested. Here too, he should have protested.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion from the mortgage case and applies it to the tree case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the mortgage case, the only way to avoid loss is that the owner protests. The same is true for the tree seller. If he stayed silent, the buyer's claim stands.
steps.whatToRemember: A buyer of a tree gets the land under it only if he claims it was included. The seller can stop this by making a מחאה, as proven from the mortgages of סורא.

phrases.english: Rather, he should have protested;
here too, he should have protested.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the proof from the mortgage case back to the tree case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: An owner who fails to protest loses his chance to stop the other person's claim, both in the mortgage case and in the tree case.

steps.title: משנה: three separate regions for חזקה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says ארץ ישראל has three separate regions for חזקה. If the owner is in one region and the holder is in another, there is no חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: There are three lands for חזקה: יהודה, עבר הירדן, and the גליל. If the owner was in יהודה and someone took possession of his field in the גליל, or the owner was in the גליל and someone took possession in יהודה, it is not a חזקה, until he is with him in one province.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that a חזקה only works if the owner and the person holding his field are in the same region.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three years of holding a field count as proof only when the owner could have protested. If the owner is in a different region, the משנה treats him as too far away, so no חזקה is made. The owner must be in the same province.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה, the start of a new משנה
Presumed ownership from holding land for three years

steps.confusionAlert: The person in יהודה or the גליל at the start is the original owner, and the one who "took possession" is a different person living on the field.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
There are three lands for presumptive ownership:
Judea, and Transjordan, and the Galilee.
If [the owner] was in Judea and [another] took possession in the Galilee,
or [the owner was] in the Galilee and [another] took possession in Judea—
it is not presumptive ownership,
until he is with him in one province.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, moving from the tree case to where the owner must be for a חזקה to work.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חזקה works only if the owner and the one holding the field are in the same one of the three regions.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: why the time is three years
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה explains that three years are required so that even an owner as far away as אספמיא can find out and come back to protest.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: They only said three years so that if the owner is in אספמיא, and someone holds his field for a year, people can go and tell him during another year, and he can come back in the following year.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives the reason for the three-year rule. It is meant to give a far-away owner enough time to hear the news and return.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Year one: someone holds the field. Year two: people travel to tell the owner. Year three: the owner comes back to protest. This reason suggests that even an owner very far away can still protect himself, which seems different from the first view in the משנה about separate regions.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the three years of חזקה are tied to giving the owner a fair chance to protest, which links back to the theme of מחאה earlier in this section.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
They only said three years
so that if he is in Spain—
and [another] holds it for a year,
people will go and inform him during a year,
and he will come back in the next year.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לֹא אָמְרוּ שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second view in the משנה, explaining the three years in a way that allows for a far-away owner.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three years are needed so that an owner even as far as אספמיא can learn of the holding and return to protest.

steps.title: What does the first opinion in the משנה hold about a protest made when the holder is not there?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the תנא קמא with a dilemma. Either way it understands מחאה שלא בפניו, the split between יהודה and גליל seems not to make sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What does the first opinion hold? Suppose he holds that a protest made when the holder is not present counts. Then even if one is in יהודה and the other is in גליל, the protest should count. Suppose instead he holds that such a protest does not count. Then even if both are in יהודה, it should not count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is questioning the first opinion in the משנה. It shows that his rule of separate regions does not seem to fit either way of understanding a protest made when the holder is not there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything depends on one question: does a protest count when the holder is not present? If it counts, the owner could have protested from יהודה to גליל, so his silence should give the holder a חזקה even across regions. If it does not count, then even within יהודה a protest made away from the holder would fail. Either way, dividing the land into regions seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גְּמָרָא; the discussion on the משנה begins here
The first opinion stated in the משנה, before רבי יהודה
He holds / he is of the opinion
A protest made when the holder of the land is not present

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is choosing one side here. It is showing that both sides seem to cause a problem for the תנא קמא, and that is the challenge.

phrases.english: GEMARA
What does the first tanna hold?
phrases.notes: This is the first opinion in the משנה, the one that said the land has three regions for חזקה (step 7).

phrases.english: If he holds that a protest made not in his presence
is a valid protest,
then even Judea and Galilee as well!
phrases.notes: He means the owner could have protested from far away, so if he stayed silent, the holder should get a חזקה even across regions.

phrases.english: If he holds that a protest made not in his presence
is not a valid protest,
then even Judea and Judea should also not work!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis of the משנה quoted in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The תנא קמא's rule that a different region prevents חזקה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dilemma: whether מחאה שלא בפניו counts or not, the division by region seems to make no difference.

steps.title: רב answers that the משנה is talking about a time of crisis
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר ממל, quoting רב, says the תנא קמא holds that מחאה שלא בפניו counts. The משנה is speaking about a שעת חירום, when news cannot pass between regions.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר ממל said in the name of רב: In truth, he holds that a protest made when the holder is not there does count. Our משנה was taught about a time of crisis.
steps.whatsHappening: רב takes the first side of the dilemma: a protest made when the holder is not there does count. He explains that the משנה is speaking about a dangerous time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, a protest made far away counts, because word of it reaches the holder. In a time of crisis, the roads between regions are cut off, so the news cannot get through. That is why being in a different region prevents a חזקה.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually / in truth (used to keep one side of a dilemma)
A time of crisis or danger, such as war

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule: a protest made when the holder is not present does count. The regions matter only when news is unable to travel.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל אָמַר רַב,
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Memel said in the name of Rav:
Actually, he holds:
a protest made not in his presence is a valid protest,
and our mishnah was taught about a time of crisis.
phrases.notes: In a time like that, travel is cut off, so word of the protest cannot reach the other region.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dilemma of step 9 by choosing its first side and limiting the משנה to a special case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the משנה to a specific situation (a time of crisis)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The regions rule seemed to contradict either view of מחאה שלא בפניו.
steps.terutzMaskana: Such a protest normally counts. The משנה speaks of a time of crisis, when the news cannot cross between regions.

steps.title: Why does the משנה mention יהודה and גליל in particular?
steps.stepSummary: If the reason is the crisis, the גמרא asks why the משנה specifically uses the example of יהודה and גליל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is special about יהודה and גליל, that the משנה mentions them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's answer. If the real problem is the crisis, why does the משנה talk about separate regions?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the issue is that roads are blocked in a time of crisis, the same problem could happen even inside one region. So why does the משנה tie the rule to יהודה and גליל? The region detail now seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: He mentioned / he chose as an example
Two of the three regions of ארץ ישראל named in the משנה

phrases.english: And what is different about Judea and Galilee
that he mentioned them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's answer in step 10 based on the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's explanation that the משנה speaks of a time of crisis
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the crisis is the cause, the same rule should apply within one region, so naming separate regions seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The גמרא begins to explain what the mention of יהודה and גליל teaches
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens its answer with 'this is what it teaches us.' The actual lesson continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it teaches us:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its answer to why the משנה mentions יהודה and גליל. The lesson itself comes at the start of the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'הא קא משמע לן' tells us the example was chosen on purpose, to teach something new. The גמרא will now explain what that lesson is.

phrases.english: This is what it teaches us:
phrases.notes: The lesson itself comes at the start of the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the challenge in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains that the wording of the משנה was chosen to teach a lesson (continues in the next lines)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Naming יהודה and גליל seemed unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: The example was chosen to teach a specific point, which the גמרא will spell out next.
